newsitem.title: TAIWAN: China spies on Taiwan's fighter deployment -paper.
newsitem.headline: China spies on Taiwan's fighter deployment -paper.

text.p: Taiwan's security authorities are on alert over apparent spying by Chinese vessels on Taiwan's deployment of French-made Mirage fighter planes recently delivered to the island, a newspaper said on Thursday.

Vessels disguised as Chinese fishing boats, but with an unusually large number of antennae, have been seen off Taiwan's northern county of Hsinchu, where five recently arrived Mirage jets are to be based, the China Times reported.

The paper, quoting an unidentified source, said the number of vessels had increased rapidly in the past few days, prompting Taiwan security authorities to suspect that they were conducting surveillance.
The boats have not intruded into Taiwan's territorial waters, but have stayed close to the area, the paper said.
The paper said when two U.S. F-16 fighter jets arrived at the southern Taiwan air base of Chiayi on April 14, the number of Chinese boats also increased in the sea nearby.
Taiwan's defence ministry declined to comment on the report.
Taiwan on May 5 took delivery of five of 60 Mirage jets it has ordered from France.

It also took delivery on Thursday of three more F-16 fighters which, together with two that arrived in April, were expected to strengthen Taiwan's air force combat power in the face of continued military threats from arch-rival China.

Taiwan in 1992 bought 150 F-16s from the United States and 60 Mirages from France in deals that outraged China, which views the island as a rebel-held province subject to eventual reunification with the mainland.
China threatens to attack Taiwan, which split from the mainland at the end of a civil war in 1949, if the island tries to declare formal independence.
